- Procurement (David): we can do separate invoices per phase; we just need each invoice to reference the master PO number. I’ll confirm the exact PO number once legal is comfortable.
- Legal (me): we reviewed the attached order form and the MSA redline. Most commercial edits look standard; two items that need attention:

  2) Indemnity carve-out — we need to preserve paragraph (b) that excludes certain third-party claims unless there is willful misconduct.

I’ve attached our internal comment file (we’ll send a clean redline later). Can you confirm whether Redwood can accept a 30-day cache retention window and if we can add a mutual step-in for security incidents?

Thanks Elena — good points. A few clarifications from Redwood legal/business:

- Cache retention: we can accept a 30-day cache retention window for ephemeral KV/prefix cache, with an explicit carve-out for logs/telemetry that we keep for operational troubleshooting up to 90 days. We’ll add language to limit cache to inference-related artifacts only.
- Indemnity: we are generally aligned on a mutual indemnity but won’t accept broad willful-misconduct exclusions that are undefined. Karthik (cc’d) will propose a narrow compromise that preserves TerraWorks’ carve-outs while protecting Redwood for third-party model-output claims.

I’ve attached our working PDF redline (MSA_redline_rkim_20271001.pdf) with inline edits — redlines starting on p.3 for the data section and p.6 for indemnity.

Next step from our side: Karthik will send proposed indemnity language by EOD Monday (10/4). If that’s acceptable, Rachel — can you confirm DocuSign split (two-envelope approach) so procurement can expect the workflow?

Elena — forwarding a compact compromise below that Kimberly and I discussed. Please review and tell us if this preserves your carve-outs. If helpful, we can mark it up in tracked changes.

--- Forwarded message ---
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-10-03T08:20:00-07:00
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
Subject: proposed indemnity language

Proposed paragraph (to replace current indemnity para b):
"Each party shall indemnify, defend and hold harmless the other from third-party claims arising out of (i) the indemnifying party’s breach of applicable law or willful misconduct, and (ii) infringement claims based on the indemnifying party’s materials. Notwithstanding the foregoing, neither party shall be liable to the other for indirect, punitive or speculative damages except in cases of gross negligence or willful misconduct. For model-output related claims, Redwood will provide reasonable cooperation but will not be liable for customer-directed outputs where customer inputs directly caused the output."

Rationale: narrows the carve-out while preserving TerraWorks’ need to exclude collateral third-party claims where TerraWorks did not contribute.

Action: if TerraWorks accepts this language in principle, we’ll incorporate into the redline and circulate a one-page summary for your GC to sign off.

Karthik

From: Elena Morales <elena@terraworks.com>

Karthik / Kimberly — thank you, that language is much closer. Two final asks before we can sign:
1) Add a clause that explicitly preserves TerraWorks’ right to defend claims that arise from customer integration code (i.e., if an internal TerraWorks script caused model outputs that triggered a claim). That keeps the allocation clear.
2) Please include the 30-day cache retention language as Kimberly outlined and define "cache" in the MSA schedule.

If Redwood can add those two items, TerraWorks is comfortable with the rest and we can proceed to DocuSign. I’ll coordinate with procurement/David for the PO number once the redline is final.

Elena
